transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (Aster - Head of ML), Trevor King (Aster - SRE), Nadia Ahmed (Aster - PM)

Summary:
Quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed go/no-go thresholds for latency/throughput/quality, reporting format (CSV + dashboard), and timeline for baseline benchmarks. SE will run hosted baseline and share results. Customer to provide sample dataset and traffic profile. Follow-up go/no-go meeting scheduled.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, security & VPC, reporting format

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we will keep this tight, purpose today is to sign off on the POC success criteria and acceptance tests so we can start the pilot next week.
00:12 Maria: Yep, thanks Samir. I have Nadia and Trevor on the call, we just want to make sure the thresholds are realistic for production like things we see now.
00:20 Samir: Totally. Jia and I ran through the initial doc you sent, tweaked a couple numbers. Jia you want to take us through the acceptance checklist?
00:28 Jia: Sure. So main buckets: latency, throughput, quality/regression, cost target, and security/compliance checks. For latency we propose P95 under 250ms for the 512 token avg payload in our hosted environment, 200ms if we run on dedicated. That is the go/no-go threshold unless we agree on higher for some heavy prompt routes.
00:48 Maria: 250ms P95 sounds aggressive but plausible. What's the baseline we measured internally?
00:54 Maria: (talking over) Our current in-house calls average around 300-350ms P95 on their smaller model.
00:59 Trevor: yeah that's true, depends a lot on encoding and batch sizes, our median is good but tails suck.
01:09 Jia: Right, and the POC plan includes both single-request latency and 1-minute sustained throughput tests. For throughput we thought 80 requests/sec sustained with 95% success under error budget; burst to 200rps for short periods. We can adjust if your profile is different.
01:28 Nadia: For our customer-facing routes the median sequence length is closer to 420 tokens, but some long background jobs hit 1k tokens. We should define scenarios.
01:38 Samir: Good call — we'll list scenarios: short-chat (<=128 tokens), mid (256-512), long (>=768). The acceptance must pass each scenario's thresholds.
01:47 Maria: And quality — how will you measure regression vs our current model?
01:51 Jia: We will use your labeled prompt set (you said ~1,200 prompts) and compute top-level metrics: correctness rate, hallucination count normalized per 1000 responses, and a human eval sample. The pass criteria: no more than 2% absolute drop in correctness and hallucination rate improvement or no more than 1% increase. We'll include a small hand-eval of 100 items.
02:14 Trevor: Is the hand-eval done by Redwood or us? We have synthetic labels but want independent scoring.
02:18 Samir: Proposal: you run first-pass automated scoring, we do the blinded human eval for the 100 sample and share results. That covers bias concerns too.
02:27 Maria: Ok. What about cost targets? We need to make sure the POC shows reasonable unit economics.
02:32 Jia: For cost we will report estimated per-1k-token cost on our hosted tier and on a dedicated baseline. Threshold is not a hard stop but an agreed target: <= $7 per 1M tokens on hosted for this workload after caching and batching assumptions; dedicated expected to be lower. If cost is >2x your current infra economics, that's a red flag for scale.
02:53 Nadia: Can you clarify the caching assumptions? We have a lot of repeated prompts so prefix caching helps.
02:58 Jia: We assume prefix/KV caching with at least 20% hit ratio for chat-like flows, and we will measure effective token reduction and show both raw token counts and cached-savings.
03:10 Samir: On reporting format — we will provide a CSV with per-scenario metrics: timestamps, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, success rate, token counts, cost estimates, and then a dashboards link for time series. Also include raw logs for the 1-hour load test. Is that acceptable?
03:26 Maria: CSV + dashboard is fine. We'll want a standard column ordering and the ability to import into our BI tool.
03:32 Jia: We'll send a schema, quick sample CSV.
03:36 Trevor: Security — we need VPC, SAML SSO, audit logs. Also SOC2 reports.
03:41 Samir: Yep, SOC2 + ISO rolling. For Private/Dedicated customers we can do VPC peering and customer KMS. For the hosted pilot we can enable dedicated tenancy if needed but that affects timelines.
03:52 Nadia: For this POC we prefer to start hosted but with VPC peering if possible. How long to enable that?
03:57 Samir: Typically 5-7 business days for basic peering config; for recorded proofs and KMS it can be longer. But for the pilot we can do tokenized TLS with audit logs and then move to peering in week two.
04:10 Maria: Ok. Back to bench—how will the baseline be run? We want both your hosted and a dedicated sim if possible.
04:16 Jia: Plan: first-run is hosted small variant to establish baseline and ensure parity of response quality. We'll run: (a) synthetic single-request latency test (1k samples), (b) 1-hour sustained ramp test with traffic profile you provide, (c) the correctness eval on the 1,200 prompt set. We'll measure CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratios.
04:37 Trevor: For the 1-hour ramp test what load shape? We have diurnal peaks but for POC use a 15-min ramp to target and then steady for 30 minutes, then a spike.
04:48 Jia: That works. We'll document the exact ramp script. For load we used target 80rps earlier, so sample test will run to 100rps spike.
04:57 Maria: Will you include per-request trace IDs so we can match logs?
04:59 Jia: Yes, we'll push a trace ID and include it in CSV.
05:04 Samir: Let's nail the go/no-go criteria explicitly so we can sign off now. Jia?
05:09 Jia: Ok, formalizing: Pass if all three buckets pass: Latency: P95 <= 250ms (hosted) across short/mid scenarios; Throughput: sustain 80rps with success rate >= 95% and error budget < 0.5% during steady state; Quality: no more than 2% absolute drop in correctness vs your baseline and hand-eval pass on the 100-sample with >=90% agreement; Cost: estimated per-1M-token cost within 2x of target (<= $14 in worst case) — cost alone doesn't block but flags commercial discussion; Security: no unresolved blockers for VPC/peering and audit logs present. If any critical security item fails it's a hard stop.
05:49 Maria: That sounds clear. Can we add p99 latency for the long scenario to be below 900ms? Our ops team worried about long-tail.
05:58 Jia: Sure add p99 < 900ms for long scenario. We'll annotate tradeoffs in the report.
06:04 Trevor: For error budgeting — what counts as error? 5xx from the service, timeouts above 30s, or malformed response?
06:12 Samir: We'll count server 5xx and client timeouts >10s as errors for the benchmark, and also include a second column for degraded responses (like safety blocks).
06:21 Maria: Great. Timelines then — when can we see the hosted baseline results?
06:24 Jia: If we get the sample dataset and traffic profile by Friday 2025-05-23, SE will run the hosted baseline early next week and share the initial report by Tuesday 2025-05-27. Then we can run the dedicated baseline the following week if you want.
06:38 Maria: Yes please do both if possible. We'll prioritize hosted but want the dedicated numbers too.
06:44 Samir: I'll get the success criteria doc out today, with the CSV schema and reporting format. Jia will run the benchmark and attach the raw logs. We will add the go/no-go signoff template to the doc so the final sync can be quick.
06:56 Trevor: About load generation — do you need a private runner in our VPC to simulate network characteristics?
07:01 Jia: We can run from Redwood's load agents but if you want exact network conditions we can run a small harness inside your VPC; that requires a short setup with your infra folks.
07:12 Trevor: I'll check windows for that. Could be useful for p99.
07:16 Nadia: One more on reporting — can we get per-route breakdown as well? Some routes are heavy and some are light, aggregated numbers hide issues.
07:22 Samir: Yep we'll include per-route and per-scenario sheets in the CSV.
07:27 Maria: Also include sampling of raw outputs for the human eval so we can audit potential hallucinations.
07:31 Jia: Yep, we'll attach a subset of responses with trace IDs.
07:34 Samir: Any blockers on compliance?
07:36 Maria: We need SOC2 docs and an initial data flow diagram. Also SAML metadata to integrate with our IdP later.
07:44 Samir: I'll attach SOC2 and a draft data flow. SAML can be done in parallel; for the pilot we can use temporary accounts.
07:51 Nadia: Ok that works.
07:53 Maria: Cool. Let's confirm dates and owners now?
07:56 Samir: Action items — Samir to send final doc by 2025-05-21; Jia to run hosted baseline and deliver report by 2025-05-27; Maria to provide dataset by 2025-05-23; Trevor to check VPC runner and contact infra by 2025-05-22. Any objections?
08:14 Maria: No objections. Sounds good.
08:16 Nadia: No objections.
08:17 Samir: Great. I think we can call sign-off on the success criteria if everyone is aligned. Maria you ok to say yes?
08:24 Maria: Yes, Aster Digital signs off on the documented success criteria assuming the timelines we discussed.
08:30 Samir: Awesome. Quick note on deliverables: we'll send the CSV schema, the bench script, and a go/no-go template. Then schedule the 30-min sync on 2025-05-29 to review results.
08:42 Trevor: Works for me.
08:44 Samir: Anything else?
08:45 Maria: One last question — if the hosted baseline fails on latency but quality is good, do we stop?
08:52 Jia: Not an automatic stop. We'll identify mitigations — batching config, quantized variant, or dedicated nodes. If mitigations can't hit thresholds within agreed remediation window (5 business days) then we escalate to commercial.
09:05 Maria: Fair.
09:07 Samir: Alright thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
09:12 [end of call]

Notes on transcription: some words auto-transcribed slightly off, e.g., "KV cache" sometimes shown as "CV cache" in the raw logs. Speaker overlaps at 00:54 and 07:01 had minor crosstalk.

Attachments/References mentioned: CSV schema (will be shared), success-criteria doc (to be sent by Samir), SOC2 report link (provided after call), bench script (to be attached by Jia).

Acceptance test checklist (human-readable consolidation):
- Scenarios: short (<=128 tokens), mid (256-512), long (>=768)
- Latency: P95 <= 250ms hosted (per scenario), P99 < 900ms for long scenario
- Throughput: sustain 80 rps with >=95% success, spike to 200rps tolerable
- Quality: automated correctness within 2% of baseline; hand-eval 100-sample >=90% agreement
- Cost: report per-1M-token cost; flag if >2x target (alert), no immediate block unless security fails
- Security: VPC/peering or equivalent audit logs; SOC2 artifacts required
- Reporting: CSV with per-route and per-scenario metrics, trace IDs, raw logs, dashboard link

End of transcript.
